### Webhooks
You can now document the webhooks your API sends. Decorate the payload Schema with `@api.webhook` or `@router.webhook` and it appears in the OpenAPI 3.1 `webhooks` section, so Swagger and Redoc show it next to your operations. This is documentation only: Ninja doesn't send anything. The [guide](https://django-ninja.dev/guide/webhooks/) shows one way to deliver them with Django tasks.

```python
from ninja import NinjaAPI, Router, Schema

api = NinjaAPI()

@api.webhook("order.paid")
class OrderPaid(Schema):
    id: int
    total: Decimal

router = Router(tags=["orders"])

@router.webhook  # name defaults to the class name: "OrderShipped"
class OrderShipped(Schema):
    id: int
```

### New documentation (and docs for AI assistants)
The docs at [django-ninja.dev](https://django-ninja.dev) are reorganized into four sections:
- **Quick Start**: build an events API in three pages
- **Tutorial**: build TaskFlow, a team task tracker, in eight parts. It covers relations, validation, JWT auth and permissions, filtering, uploads, testing, OpenAPI polish and versioning
- **Guide**: one short page per topic, and every example was run against the current code
- **About**

The docs now include files for LLMs. Point your coding assistant at [`/llms.txt`](https://django-ninja.dev/llms.txt), which has usage notes and a link to every page, or at [`/llms-full.txt`](https://django-ninja.dev/llms-full.txt), which is the whole Guide in one file. Every page is also served as raw Markdown, e.g. [`/guide/routers.md`](https://django-ninja.dev/guide/routers.md).

### `register_field()` accepts field classes
A custom Django field that subclasses a built-in one inherits its internal type, so registering it by name (`"UUIDField"`) would change every `UUIDField`. You can now register the field class itself:

```python
from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import BeforeValidator
from ninja.orm import register_field

class PublicIDField(models.UUIDField):
    def from_db_value(self, value, expression, connection):
        return PublicID(value)

register_field(PublicIDField, Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(str)])
```

The registration also applies to subclasses, and the most specific class wins. It also covers ForeignKey and OneToOne fields that point at that field. Forward FK and OneToOne fields now take their type from the `to_field` target instead of always using the related model's pk.

### Optional schema parameters
An `Optional` schema used as a `Query`, `Header` or `Form` param now falls back to its default when none of its fields are sent:

```python
class Filters(Schema):
    city: str
    year: int = 2026

@api.get("/events")
def events(request, filters: Filters | None = Query(None)):
    ...

# GET /events            -> filters is None   (was 422)
# GET /events?city=Kyiv  -> Filters(city="Kyiv", year=2026)
```

### `Body` params next to files
When you mix `Body` params with `File` or `Form`, each multipart part is now read the way Swagger and generated clients send it. Primitive types (`str`, `int`, `date`, `Enum`, `EmailStr`, ...) are read as plain text, and objects and arrays are read as JSON:

```python
@api.post("/upload")
def upload(
    request,
    file: File[UploadedFile],
    note: str = Body(...),
    day: date = Body(...),
    meta: dict[str, int] | None = Body(None),
):
    ...

# note='say "hi"'  day=2024-01-02  meta='{"a": 1}'  -> 200 (quoted strings and dates used to give 400)
```

### ModelSchema improvements
Model fields now always come first, in model order, followed by your custom fields. A field you declare on the schema is used as-is, so a third-party model field that Ninja can't convert no longer breaks `fields = "__all__"`:

`

^ Please read ^

Fast to learn, fast to code, fast to run

![Test](https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/actions/workflows/test_full.yml/badge.svg) ![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/codecov/c/github/vitalik/django-ninja) [![PyPI version](https://badge.fury.io/py/django-ninja.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/py/django-ninja) [![Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/personalized-badge/django-ninja?period=month&units=international_system&left_color=black&right_color=brightgreen&left_text=downloads/month)](https://pepy.tech/project/django-ninja) # Django Ninja - Fast Django REST Framework **Django Ninja** is a web framework for building APIs with **Django** and Python 3.6+ **type hints**. **Key features:** - **Easy**: Designed to be easy to use and intuitive. - **FAST execution**: Very high performance thanks to **Pydantic** and **async support**. - **Fast to code**: Type hints and automatic docs lets you focus only on business logic. - **Standards-based**: Based on the open standards for APIs: **OpenAPI** (previously known as Swagger) and **JSON Schema**. - **Django friendly**: (obviously) has good integration with the Django core and ORM. - **Production ready**: Used by multiple companies on live projects (If you use django-ninja and would like to publish your feedback, please email ppr.vitaly@gmail.com). ![Django Ninja REST Framework](docs/docs/img/benchmark.png) **Documentation**: https://django-ninja.dev --- ## Installation ``` pip install django-ninja ``` ## Usage In your django project next to urls.py create new `api.py` file: ```Python from ninja import NinjaAPI api = NinjaAPI() @api.get("/add") def add(request, a: int, b: int): return {"result": a + b} ``` Now go to `urls.py` and add the following: ```Python hl_lines="3 7" ... from .api import api urlpatterns = [ path("admin/", admin.site.urls), path("api/", api.urls), # <---------- ! ] ``` **That's it !** Now you've just created an API that: - receives an HTTP GET request at `/api/add` - takes, validates and type-casts GET parameters `a` and `b` - decodes the result to JSON - generates an OpenAPI schema for defined operation ### Interactive API docs Now go to http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/docs You will see the automatic interactive API documentation (provided by Swagger UI or Redoc): ![Swagger UI](docs/docs/img/index-swagger-ui.png) ## Sponsors Become a sponsor ## What next? - Read the full documentation here - https://django-ninja.dev - To support this project, please give star it on Github. ![github star](docs/docs/img/github-star.png) - Share it [via Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Check%20out%20Django%20Ninja%20-%20Fast%20Django%20REST%20Framework%20-%20https%3A%2F%2Fdjango-ninja.dev) - If you already using django-ninja, please share your feedback to ppr.vitaly@gmail.com
